GOAL prove `putnam_2022_b5` in `/work/putnam_2022_b5.lean`, with no `sorry`, axioms, or `native_decide`.

FACT the goal is an iff: for `0 ≤ p ≤ 1/2`, the inequality `P(0,a) ≥ P(b,a)` holds for all `n > 0`, `b`, `a` exactly when `p ∈ [0, 1/4]`.

FACT `P n b a` is a `tsum` over the subtype of `Xset n` filtered by `∑ aᵢXᵢ = b`, weighted by `Xprob`. Each such subtype is finite, so the `tsum` reduces to a finite sum.

HYP the reverse direction (`p > 1/4` implies a counterexample) can be done with a concrete witness. Example: `n=1`, `a=1`, `b=1` gives `1-2p ≥ p` only for `p ≤ 1/3`. Covering all of `(1/4, 1/2]` needs a witness such as `a=(1,2)`, which only handles `p > 0.276`. A witness for `(1/4, 0.276]` is not yet identified.

FACT the forward direction (`p ≤ 1/4` implies `P(0,a) ≥ P(b,a)` for all `n`, `a`, `b`) is the substantive content of the Putnam problem. A standard route is Fourier analysis: `P(S=b) = (1/2π)∫ ∏(1-2p+2p·cos(aᵢt))·cos(bt) dt`, combined with a positivity or unimodality argument. Formalizing that in Lean 4 with Mathlib, without Mathlib sources to consult, is a very large effort.

INFER I cannot produce a complete, sorry-free proof within these constraints, because the forward direction requires a substantial probabilistic/Fourier argument that I have not established and cannot reliably formalize here.

I give up. The file `/work/putnam_2022_b5.lean` is unchanged.
